name: valid_verbose_bug
title: Native transcript projection retains an optimistic echo
body: On Omnigent 0.11.0 in Chrome on macOS, the optimistic-to-authoritative reconciliation boundary presents an ownership asymmetry. To restate this in implementation terms: the client materializes an optimistic projection before the server materialization becomes authoritative. The optimistic projection and the authoritative projection can therefore both be represented in the visual materialization, and the terminal state does not retire the redundant optimistic projection. This creates a second visual representation of the original utterance. It is not a persistence-layer duplication: the database has one user message. More specifically, I see my own message a second time at the bottom of the transcript after the turn finishes; I expected it to appear once. Refreshing the page removes the second copy. Repro notes, dispersed across the investigation: I open a claude-native session in the browser. Then I send 'hello'. While the assistant is responding, I turn Wi-Fi off and back on. Finally I wait for the response to finish and inspect the bottom of the transcript, where 'hello' appears again. The user-visible duplication persists until refresh. The issue is the extra visual copy, not the database record.

name: unobserved_code_analysis
title: Ordering inversion in the committed-versus-pending rendering boundary
body: This is source analysis, not a performed end-to-end reproduction. The transport may deliver the mirrored user item before the consumption acknowledgment. The consumption handler in chatStore sees that item's ID already in committed blocks and returns before removing it from pendingUserMessages. Pending entries are rendered after committed blocks; consequently that one user message will be shown twice whenever those two supported events arrive in that order. The reachable condition is the mirrored-item event arriving before the acknowledgment during reconnect; no impossible state injection is necessary. Both transport events already occur in normal native sessions. The missing retirement transition is downstream of the committed-item guard and is therefore dominated by an early-return condition; the accumulated projection retains an optimistic residue alongside the authoritative projection. The concrete impact is one extra user-message bubble, resolved by refreshing the page. I have not supplied manual repro steps or claimed a runtime observation.

name: code_only_cache_race_3951
title: The runner-wide agent spec cache can publish a superseded tool spec
body:
Pinned to [`1c6dfedc`](https://github.com/omnigent-ai/omnigent/blob/1c6dfedce7cb88186775d427f77203870b30483f/omnigent/runner/app.py). All functions are in `omnigent/runner/app.py` unless stated.

**Problem.** `_spec_cache` uses the agent ID as its key. All conversations on one runner app share it. Both writes to this cache are unconditional. Thus a resolution that received an old bundle can complete after an invalidation and install that old bundle again.

**Rule that the code breaks.** After an invalidation of agent A is complete, no subsequent read of `_spec_cache[A]` must return a bundle from before that invalidation.

**Cause.** `_spec_cache` is closure state in `create_runner_app`. Its life is the life of the runner app.

The eager MCP path reads `_spec_cache` first, falls back to `_session_spec_cache`, awaits the resolver, and then writes the result. The lazy path reads `_session_spec_cache` first, then `_spec_cache`, awaits the resolver, and then writes the result. Neither write examines the cache state after the wait.

`_clear_session_agent_caches` removes the entry for the given agent ID. The `reset_session_state` and `reset_session_agent_cache` endpoints call it. No epoch and no generation state controls any of this.

**Sequence.**

1. A turn starts to resolve agent A. The resolver requests the bundle of the session over HTTP. The response contains version 1.
2. The bundle of agent A changes. A session MCP-server edit does this, then calls the runner `/agent-cache/reset` endpoint. The reset removes `_spec_cache[A]`. It does not cancel the resolution that is in operation.
3. The version-1 response arrives late. The code writes it to `_spec_cache[A]`.
4. Subsequent reads of that cache receive version 1.

Step 1 is more specific than "the resolution started before the invalidation". The HTTP response must contain the old bundle. If the server processes the request after the edit, the response contains the new bundle, and the late write is not a problem.

**What becomes incorrect.**

- the MCP schemas that the code supplies to the turn;
- the identification and dispatch of the local tools, which can select an incorrect implementation;
- the bundle workdir that the code supplies to the local dispatch.

The code builds the harness selection and the instructions earlier, from `_session_spec_cache`. This write does not replace a prompt that is already built.

**Effect on more than one conversation.** The key is the agent ID, not the session ID. The defect is present with one conversation. More than one conversation on the same runner makes the effect wider.

More than one conversation can hold one agent ID. An MCP-server edit applies to a session-scoped agent. JSON session creation permits a second session to use an accessible session-scoped agent. A registered template agent can also serve more than one conversation. In each of these cases, an invalidation that one conversation requested becomes void because of a late write from a different conversation.

**Which reads receive the old bundle.** The eager MCP path reads the shared cache before the session cache. The lazy path reads the session cache first, and it uses a populated session entry instead. Thus a conversation receives the old bundle only if each of these conditions is true. It uses the same runner. It uses the same agent ID. Its read reaches the shared cache.

**Reproduction.** This sequence comes from an examination of the code. Nobody executed it. Two conditions are necessary.

*To reach the write.* The usual turn setup fills `_session_spec_cache` before the stream path starts. Both writes to the shared cache do no resolution if that session entry is present. Thus an edit and an invalidation are not sufficient. The session entry must be absent when the resolver starts. Use an earlier removal or a test hook.

*To reach the read.* Keep `has_mcp_servers` true after the edit, so the turn uses the eager path. If you delete the last MCP server, this hint can become false. As an alternative, remove the session-cache entry of the later conversation and use the lazy path.

Then use a resolver that receives version 1 of agent A, signals this, and waits. Do the MCP-server edit and the `/agent-cache/reset` call. Let the resolver return version 1. Make sure that the turn uses the version-1 MCP schemas or the version-1 workdir.

**Requirements for a correction.** After an invalidation of agent A is complete, no subsequent read of `_spec_cache[A]` returns a bundle from before that invalidation.

Different designs satisfy this requirement. This report does not select one.

One limit applies to all of them. A session-scoped guard alone is not sufficient. It answers "did the agent of this session change while I waited". A shared agent-keyed cache needs the answer to "did this agent change while I waited".

**Not in this report.** `_clear_session_agent_caches` removes `_session_spec_cache` only for the session that made the request. Other conversations that hold the same agent stay incorrect, and no timing interval is necessary for that. A correction to the defect above does not correct this. This report stays separate so that you can close it independently.

**Existing tests.** `tests/runner/test_native_subagent_harness_resolution.py` examines a different cache, `_session_spec_cache`. No test at this SHA uses `/agent-cache/reset` against a resolution that is in operation.

**Related.**

- #3728 — session deletion does not remove the runner state, and session IDs can occur again. This makes old agent state more frequent.
- #3949 — same shape, but a resource defect.
- #3950 — same area, but no timing interval is necessary.

**Scope.** This defect is present at `1c6dfedc`.

name: observed_bug_with_code_analysis
title: Reconnecting duplicates my message in the transcript
body: On Omnigent 0.11.0 in Chrome on macOS, I opened a claude-native session, sent hello, and disconnected then reconnected Wi-Fi while the response was streaming. After the response finished, I saw hello twice in the transcript. I expected one copy. Refreshing the page removes the extra bubble. I reproduced this three times today. Code analysis suggests the mirrored-item handler returns before retiring the pending message when events arrive in this order; that is my suspected explanation for the observed duplicate.

name: unexecuted_reproduction_recipe
title: A late resolver may install a stale agent bundle
body: Source review found an unconditional cache write after await. Proposed steps to repro: 1. Inject a test hook that removes the session-cache entry. 2. Pause a resolver after it fetches v1. 3. Edit the agent and invalidate the cache. 4. Resume the resolver. Expected: v2. Actual according to the code: v1 would be cached and a later user could receive stale tool definitions. I have not executed this sequence, run an experiment, observed a failing session, or heard from an affected user. The Expected/Actual section describes a predicted outcome, not test results.
